name: Founder's Debt Day
description: Observed annually on March 14th, Founder's Debt Day commemorates the 2189 signing of the Meridian Compact, the legal instrument by which HelixCore Consolidated, Nakamura-Voss Infrastructure, and the Pelletier Group jointly incorporated the Great Lakes Corridor into what became Meridian 88. Corponation employees are required to attend mandatory 'gratitude assemblies' at their workplace hubs, during which productivity metrics from the previous fiscal year are displayed publicly alongside corporate benevolence tallies — subsidized meals provided, medical debts forgiven, housing vouchers distributed. The holiday's official name references the concept that citizens owe their safety and opportunity to the founding corponations, a framing that street culture has long rebranded with open contempt.
cultural_impact: Founder's Debt Day is the single most universally despised mandatory holiday in M88, generating more sick-day filings, underground counter-celebrations, and graffiti campaigns than any other corporate observance. Its enforcement has paradoxically become a reliable annual barometer of how much resentment each tier is accumulating toward corporate governance.
locations: HelixCore Central Atrium, Tier 4 Spine District
The Rust Nave (counter-celebration site), Tier 1 South Shelf
story_hooks: A leaked internal HelixCore document reveals that the Meridian Compact was actually signed under duress — the founding corponations had evidence of a pre-existing disaster they allowed to happen to justify the incorporation, and someone is trying to release it on Founder's Debt Day for maximum exposure.

A Tier 2 assembly worker is selected to give the 'citizen gratitude speech' at this year's mandatory rally — but she has been secretly radicalized by Shelf organizer Temi Osei-Asante and must decide whether to deliver the script or speak the truth in front of forty thousand people and live feeds.
The Rust Nave's annual counter-celebration is infiltrated by a corporate monitor who gradually finds themselves moved by what they witness — and must choose between their report and their conscience.
origin_event: The signing of the Meridian Compact on March 14, 2189, which legally consolidated the Great Lakes Corridor under joint corponation governance and dissolved the last municipal government structures inherited from pre-Collapse Chicago and Milwaukee.
tier_observations: Tier 5 executives host private gala dinners in Spire sky-clubs, toasting with genuine aged spirits and receiving bonus distributions framed as 'dividend gratitude.' Tier 4 employees attend polished assemblies with catered food and performance reviews tied to their attendance enthusiasm scores. Tier 3 workers sit through mandatory holo-presentations in break rooms, most with BCIs quietly tuned to background entertainment. Tier 2 workers clock mandatory unpaid attendance hours and receive a single subsidized meal voucher. Tier 1 residents, many of whom have no corporate employer, are largely ignored by enforcement — and use the day for the Rust Nave counter-celebration, a raucous, defiant block gathering where the Compact is read aloud mockingly and burned in effigy.
